title: Fourier coefficient of the square
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $S$ be a nonempty subset of the coordinates whose Fourier coefficient for $f$ is nonzero. Suppose every nonempty subset $T$ with nonzero Fourier coefficient for $f$ satisfies $2n<3|T|$. Then the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the pointwise square $f^2$ equals twice the product of the constant Fourier coefficient of $f$ and its Fourier coefficient at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is nonzero
